title: curl as a debugging tool
objectives: Predict what `-i`, `-v`, `-s` and `-o` show, and which parts go to stdout and which to stderr
Say what `-d` does to the method and `Content-Type`, and send JSON with `--json` (curl 7.82.0+) or explicit headers
Quote JSON, URLs and variables correctly in zsh and bash, and use `--data-raw` to avoid the `@` file trap
Replay a signup → login → authenticated request, carrying a bearer token and cookies with `-c`/`-b`
Predict what `-X` and `-L` change on the wire, and make a script fail when the server returns a `5xx`

sources.title: curl changelog (8.3.0: missing input file is an error)

questions.prompt: `curl -d 'name=ada' https://api.example.com/users` — what method and `Content-Type` go out?

options.text: `POST` with `Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded`
`GET` with `?name=ada` appended to the URL
`POST` with `Content-Type: text/plain`
`POST` with no `Content-Type` — curl leaves labelling to you

questions.explanation: `-d` sends data "in the same way that a browser does when a user has filled in an HTML form": the method becomes `POST` and curl adds the form content type. Putting data in the query string is what `-G` does. `text/plain;charset=UTF-8` is `fetch`'s default for a string body, not curl's.

questions.prompt: `curl -d '{"email":"ada@example.com"}' http://localhost:4123/auth/signup` gets `400 email is required` from an Express API using `express.json()`. The JSON is valid. Why?

options.text: `-d` labels the body `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`, so the JSON parser skips it — use `--json`
The JSON must be wrapped in double quotes, not single quotes
`-d` sends a `GET`, and `GET` bodies are ignored
curl strips the braces from data that isn't a file

questions.explanation: The bytes on the wire are exactly the JSON — but the `Content-Type` says form, and body parsers trust the label, not the content. `--json` (curl 7.82.0+) sends `Content-Type: application/json` and `Accept: application/json`; on older curl add `-H 'Content-Type: application/json'`. Single quotes are the *right* choice for literal JSON in the shell.

questions.prompt: You suspect your `Authorization` header never actually goes out. Which flag shows you?

options.text: `-v` — the lines starting with `>` are the request curl sent
`-i` — it prints the headers
`-I` — it prints only headers, so it's easier to read
`-s` — it removes the noise so headers stand out

questions.explanation: `-i` prints the *response* headers only; it can't tell you what was sent. `-I` sends a different request (`HEAD`) and also shows only the response. `-v` prints both directions: `>` for sent, `<` for received, `*` for curl's notes. (`-s` hides the progress meter and errors; it shows nothing extra.)

questions.prompt: `TOKEN` holds a valid access token, yet `curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' http://localhost:4123/me` returns `401` with `error="invalid_token"`. Why?

options.text: Single quotes stop the shell expanding `$TOKEN`, so the server receives the literal text `$TOKEN`
The token expired between the two commands
The scheme must be lowercase: `bearer`
Bearer tokens must be sent with `--oauth2-bearer`, not `-H`

questions.explanation: The shell expands `$VAR` inside double quotes and leaves it alone inside single quotes. Use `-H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"`. The auth scheme is case-insensitive in HTTP, and `--oauth2-bearer` is just a shortcut for the same header. An expired token would also be `invalid_token` — which is why `-v` (showing the `> Authorization:` line) is the faster way to tell the two apart.

questions.prompt: A script posts user comments with `curl -d "$COMMENT" …`. One comment is `@channel please review`. With curl 8.3.0 or later, what happens?

options.text: curl tries to read a file named `channel please review`, fails, and exits with code 26 — nothing is sent
The comment is sent as typed; `@` is only special in URLs
curl URL-encodes the `@` as `%40` and sends it
curl sends an empty `POST`

questions.explanation: For `-d`, data that **starts with** `@` is a filename to read the body from. Since curl 8.3.0 a missing file is an error (exit 26); older versions only printed a warning and sent an empty `POST` — the last option. If a file with that name existed, its contents would be posted. `--data-raw` sends the value literally.

questions.prompt: In zsh, `curl http://localhost:4123/search?q=tea` prints `zsh: no matches found: http://localhost:4123/search?q=tea` and curl never runs. What's the fix?

options.text: Quote the URL: `curl 'http://localhost:4123/search?q=tea'`
Add `-g` to switch off curl's URL globbing
Write the `?` as `%3F`
Nothing — the server is down

questions.explanation: zsh treats an unquoted `?` as a filename wildcard and, with its default `NOMATCH` option, refuses to run a command whose pattern matched no files. The error comes from the shell, so no curl flag can fix it. `%3F` would make the `?` part of the *path* (`/search%3Fq=tea`) instead of starting a query string. Quote every URL that contains `?`, `&` or `[`.

questions.prompt: A deploy step runs `curl -s https://api.example.com/health` and moves on if it exits `0`. The service is down and answers `503`. What happens?

options.text: curl exits `0`: the transfer worked, so the deploy continues — add `--fail-with-body` (or `-f`) to get exit 22 on any status of 400 or more
curl's exit code is the status, `503`, so the step fails
curl exits `1` for every `5xx`, so the step fails
`-s` hides the error; removing it makes curl exit non-zero

questions.explanation: By default curl reports on the *transfer*, not on the HTTP status: a `503` delivered intact is a success. `-f`/`--fail` exits 22 for statuses ≥ 400 and prints no body; `--fail-with-body` (curl 7.76.0+) exits 22 and keeps the body for the log. `-s` only silences the progress meter and curl's own messages.

prompts.prompt: Send this body as JSON in one flag (curl 7.82.0+).
prompts.explanation: `--json` = `--data-binary` + `Content-Type: application/json` + `Accept: application/json`, and it makes the request a `POST`. No `-X POST` needed.

prompts.prompt: The same request on a curl older than 7.82.0, with the data sent literally even if it starts with `@`.
prompts.explanation: Without the header, `-d`-style options label the body as a form. `--data-raw` is `-d` without the `@`-means-file rule; `-d` would work for this literal too, but not for a value that happens to start with `@`.

prompts.prompt: Send the captured access token. (Note the double quotes.)
prompts.explanation: `Authorization: Bearer <token>` is the RFC 6750 header form. Double quotes let the shell expand `$TOKEN`; `--oauth2-bearer "$TOKEN"` builds the same header.

prompts.prompt: Save the cookies from login, then send them (and save the rotated one) on refresh.
prompts.explanation: `-c` / `--cookie-jar` writes every cookie curl holds to the file when it finishes; `-b` / `--cookie` reads the file and sends the cookies that match the URL. Naming the same file for both carries a session across commands.

prompts.prompt: Print just the status code — no body, no progress meter.
prompts.explanation: `-w` prints variables after the transfer; `%{http_code}` (also `%{response_code}`) is the last response's status. `-o /dev/null` throws the body away and `-s` hides the meter, so the output is exactly `500`.

snippets.question: What does `head -1` print?
snippets.explanation: `-i` writes the status line and response headers into the **same** stream as the body — stdout — so the file starts with `HTTP/1.1 200 OK`. Handy for saving a whole response; a trap if a later step expects `out.txt` to be pure JSON.

snippets.question: What does `cat out.txt` print?
snippets.explanation: `-v` writes its `*`, `>` and `<` lines to **stderr**, so they appear on your screen while only the body goes into the file. That's the opposite of `-i`. To capture the conversation too, redirect stderr as well: `2> trace.txt`.

code: # /echo replies with the method and body it received
snippets.question: What method and body does `/echo` receive?
snippets.explanation: After a `301`, `302` or `303`, `-L` re-sends a `POST` as a `GET` without the body. `-X POST` forces the method *word* back to `POST` on every hop, but it doesn't bring the body back — the server gets an empty `POST` (curl 8.7.1 output: `{"method":"POST",…,"body":""}`). Drop `-X` (you get a `GET`), or redirect with `307`/`308`, which keep method and body. Since curl 8.16.0, `--follow` applies `-X` the way the spec intends.
